messages:
Maya K (ml-eng): quick share — ran a small bakeoff across FP8 / AWQ-INT8 / GPTQ (4-bit-ish) on the new 13B. mixing seq lengths (8 / 128 / 1024) to match web+api traffic. results below, then a proposed traffic-shift + canary/fallback snippet.

Samir P (infra): awesome, numbers please. TL;DR on latency vs quality?

Maya K (ml-eng): TL;DR: latency order (fastest -> slowest) = AWQ-int8 ~ FP8 < GPTQ. quality (perplexity / QA EM / rouge-ish): FP8 slightly worse on long-form (~+1.6% error), AWQ-int8 has small deltas on instruction-following (~+0.8%), GPTQ best fidelity but 2-3x token latency.

Olivia R (deploy): can you paste the perf table? even rough percent deltas is fine.

Maya K (ml-eng): perf table (median over 100 runs each):
```
model_variant, median_tok_ms (seq=128), delta_EM (qa set)
fp8, 9.2ms, +1.6%
awq-int8, 8.8ms, +0.8%
gptq-4bit, 24.5ms, +0.1%
fp32 (baseline), 22.7ms, 0.0%
```
Note: fp8 has better latency than fp32 for short sequences due to kernel path; for long seqs (1024) FP8 and GPTQ both drop to ~80-120ms token because attention cost dominates.

Henry L (sre): what's the memory footprint / batch size headroom? we need that for Dedicated sizing.

Maya K (ml-eng): memory summary (rough): FP8: -38% params mem vs fp32; AWQ-int8: -42%; GPTQ-4bit: -55% but chunked KV can blow out runtime mem on long prompts. Batch headroom: AWQ-int8 allows +1.5x batch for same GPU.

Elena S (product): any quality regressions on the safety/golden set? we need gating thresholds before rollout.

Maya K (ml-eng): ran golden set (500 prompts): FP8 fails 12 cases (mostly hallucination length), AWQ-int8 fails 6, GPTQ fails 2. I recommend gate = max allowed delta 1.0% EM or 8 regressions on golden. AWQ-int8 is within gate, FP8 is borderline.

Samir P (infra): ok. proposal: host AWQ-int8 as primary in Hosted for latency/cost win, enable GPTQ-4bit as fallback for quality regressions; Dedicated customers can opt-in to GPTQ or FP32. Suggest staged rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with golden-check after each ramp. Can we encode auto-fallback if regressions spike?

Maya K (ml-eng): yes — we tested rollback triggers. here's a sample rollout policy patch (pseudo-Redwood YAML):
```yaml
rollout_policy:
  variant: awq-int8
  stages:
    - pct: 1
      duration: 4h
      checks:
        - golden_delta_max: 0.01
        - p95_latency_max_ms: 120
    - pct: 5
      duration: 12h
    - pct: 20
      duration: 24h
    - pct: 100
      duration: 72h
  fallback_on_fail: gptq-4bit
  canary_region: us-west-2
  dedicated_override: allow_opt_in(gptq-4bit, fp32)
```
If golden_delta or latency breach, auto-fallback to gptq-4bit for that request corridor, and raise alert to #eng-oncall.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary -> awq-int8 @ 1767897200 (1% for 4h). User: Olivia R (deploy).

Olivia R (deploy): I'll kick off canary tomorrow 09:00 PT. can someone own smoke evals and the golden checks during ramp?

Maya K (ml-eng): I'll run the golden set and the QA harness first 30m of canary, then hourly checks. Will post a short report to the thread.

Henry L (sre): I'll wire the alert if p95 latency > 140ms or error rate > 0.7% in that corridor. also adding a circuit-breaker to reduce traffic to hosted fallback pool.

Elena S (product): product ok with AWQ-int8 as default for hosted if it stays within gating. Please capture user-visible cost delta for next quarter.

Samir P (infra): note for private deployments: customers with strict determinism must remain on FP32 or GPTQ (explicit opt-in). we'll add a flag in private provisioning UI.

Maya K (ml-eng): post-canary checklist: publish per-route perf curves, update model catalog entry with quant-profile and recommended workloads, annotate known failure modes (long hallucination edgecases for FP8).

Olivia R (deploy): thanks — let's sync on rollout postmortem 48h after 100% roll.

Maya K (ml-eng): ACK. I'll drop the first smoke results in ~2hrs. :rocket:
